r.정치 구도: A one-party state led by the Communist Party. The party general secretary holds the most power, in a collective leadership in which the state president, the prime minister and the chair of the National Assembly have shared power. In recent years an anti-corruption campaign has forced out a state president and one senior figure after another, and reforms have sharply cut government bodies and local administrative units. Party congresses held every five years set the leadership and economic direction. It has grown fast since embracing a market economy with the 1986 'Doi Moi' reforms.

t.why: It has emerged as an alternative production base to China, and electronics companies such as Samsung and Apple's suppliers have moved factories there. Under its 'bamboo diplomacy' it keeps up relations with the United States, China and Russia alike, and in 2023 it raised relations with the United States to the highest level. Its long coastline faces the South China Sea, where it confronts China over the Paracel and Spratly islands. A core member of ASEAN, it belongs to many free trade agreements and is highly dependent on exports.
t.rel: It has deep ties with China as a fellow communist state but disputes islands in the South China Sea. It raised relations with the United States, its former enemy, to the highest level in 2023, and it is a core member of ASEAN.
t.korea: The two established relations in 1992, and Vietnam is roughly Korea's third-largest trading partner. A large part of Samsung's smartphones are made in Vietnam, and Korea is one of its largest investors. Because Korean troops fought in the Vietnam War, the issue of civilian victims is still raised. Exchanges between people run deep through international marriage, study abroad and workers, and many Vietnamese live in Korea. Places such as Da Nang and Nha Trang are favorite destinations for Korean travelers.
t.know: Vietnam is the world's second-largest coffee producer.
etext: It has drawn foreign factories with a young, nimble workforce, low wages and many free trade agreements. It makes phones, laptops, clothing, footwear and furniture for the United States, China and Europe. Foreign-invested companies produce a large share of its exports.
A large part of Samsung's global smartphone production comes from its plants in Vietnam. Korea is one of Vietnam's largest investors, and many Korean suppliers have followed.
Much of its work is assembling parts and materials imported from China and Korea, so little value added stays at home. Power shortages and US tariff pressure are also risks.
